newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian film star Mastroianni dies in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Italian film star Mastroianni dies in Paris.

text.p: Marcello Mastroianni, Italy's most famous film actor, died on Thursday at his home in Paris, his Italian agent said. He was 72.
Giovanna Cau said Mastroianni passed away on Thursday morning but she could not confirm Italian news agency reports that he had been suffering from cancer of the pancreas.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Cau said Mastroianni's two daughters were with him at the time.
"He was perhaps the greatest European cinema actor of the last 50 years," French producer Daniel Toscan du Plantier said from Paris.
Italian radio, reporting from Paris, said he had died at dawn and that friends, including many from the film world, were arriving at his house in the French capital to pay respects.
Cau said Mastroianni had continued to work in recent months. "He was an exceptional man. His main virtures were simplicity and discretion," she said, her voice breaking with emotion.
Mastroianni, one of Europe's enduring screen symbols of the Latin Lover, was Italy's most internationally recognised actor.

From his first worldwide success in director Federico Fellini's "La Dolce Vita" in 1960 to his portrayal of the ageing dancer in Fellini's "Ginger and Fred" a quarter of a century later, Mastroianni was the Italian cinema's leading male export.

Apart from "La Dolce Vita", Mastroianni perhaps will be best remembered for films in which he starred with Sophia Loren such as "Marriage Italian Style", "The Priest's Wife", "Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow", "Sunflowers" and "A Special Day."
Mastroianni, who shunned publicity and rarely granted interviews, was born to peasant parents on September 28, 1924, at Fontana Liri, a mountain hamlet southeast of Rome.
When he was still a boy the family moved to the northern industrial city of Turin and then to Rome, where Marcello finished a degree in surveying and planned to become an architect.

At 19, he was picked up by Nazi troops who had occupied Rome and sent to a forced labour camp in northern Italy. He escaped to Venice, where he drew pictures of the lagoon city's landmarks and sold them to tourists for food.

After the war he returned to Rome, where he worked as a clerk in the accounting department of the British Eagle-Lion film company and in the evenings began acting with a Rome University theatrical company.
In 1947 he made his screen debut in the Italian version of "Les Miserables" and a year later made his stage debut in a play which starred Giulietta Masina, wife of Fellini.

It was an acquaintanceship that changed his life for it was through Fellini, who was destined to become Italy's most famous director, that Mastroianni later achieved international acclaim in films such as "La Dolce Vita" and "Eight-and-a-Half" in the early 1960s.

In 1950 Mastroianni married Flora Carabella and had a daughter, Barbara. In the late 1960s he lived for a period with French film star Catherine Deneuve and had a daughter named Chiara by her in 1972.
